habitat: Shallows of large rivers, dams, estuaries and floodplains, usually a single bird standing still.
summary: A very large white egret, nearly the size of a Grey Heron, with an orange-yellow bill and entirely black legs and feet. The gape line extends behind the eye. For a few weeks when breeding the bill is black, often with a yellow base, and filamentous plumes grow on the back. It is dispersive and nomadic.

similar.note: Yellow-billed Egret is smaller. Its gape stops below the eye, and its upper legs are yellow rather than black.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 16–64.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: orange-yellow; black, often with a yellow base, for a few weeks when breeding

upperparts.pattern: Filamentous plumes on the back for a few weeks when breeding.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The texts do not separate the sexes. The catalogue cut is not labelled by sex. Grade A from France. No playable recording was filed under a Kruger locality.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a fairly common resident that is also dispersive and nomadic. The breeding bill and plumes last only a few weeks, so they were not stored as a summer plumage. Chick down is not described. The call is grade A from France.
